hypothesis: There is a discrete involution sigma on the complex numbers, distinct from a rotation, that fixes the critical line Re(s) = 1/2 and represents a genuinely new element extending C, analogous to how i extends R.
falsification_criterion: If the expression can be written as an affine combination of s and conjugate(s), it is not a new algebraic object, only a known map in unfamiliar notation. Separately: if the map treats every prime identically when probed against Euler-factor exponents p^{-s}, it carries no arithmetic content and cannot by itself explain the location of the zeta zeros.
notes: This is the sigma(s) = 1 - conjugate(s) map from the dimension-shift module: the reflection implied by the zeta functional equation zeta(s) <-> zeta(1-s), combined with conjugation.
